stem:
Boman has a paper heart with a possible mid-line drawn on it.

Which two claims correctly decide whether that mid-line is a line of symmetry?

options.text: The mid-line is a line of symmetry whenever the heart looks balanced, even if the two halves need not be folded onto each other.
Fold the heart along the mid-line; the mid-line is a line of symmetry only when the two halves overlap exactly.
Exact fold-overlap of the two halves is the test that decides the mid-line is a line of symmetry.
A line of symmetry is what creates the fold along the mid-line.

teacher.key_rationale: The fold-overlap test decides a line of symmetry. Looking balanced without folding omits the test. Saying symmetry creates the fold reverses the relation.
